books.title: The Winter Market
books.author: Yently Kids
pages: Every December, the town square filled with stalls for the Winter Market. There were lanterns, hot chocolate, and the smell of fresh bread.
This year, a girl called Hana had her own stall for the first time. She had made scarves, hats, and mittens with her grandmother.
'What if nobody buys anything?' Hana whispered nervously as the market opened. Her grandmother smiled. 'Just be kind, and the rest will follow.'
A cold wind blew, and an old man stopped at Hana's stall. He had no gloves, and his hands were red with cold. Hana gave him a pair of mittens for free.
The old man thanked her with tears in his eyes. Word spread through the market, and soon people were queuing at Hana's little stall.
By sunset, Hana had sold every scarf and hat. She used the money to buy wool, so she and her grandmother could make more for next year.
That night, Hana hung a lantern in her window. It glowed warm and bright, just like the kindness she had shared at the Winter Market.

books.title: The Storm Runner
books.author: Yently Kids
pages: In a village by the sea lived a girl called Ines, who was the fastest runner in the whole county. She could outrun the wind itself, people said.
One evening, a great storm gathered over the sea. The fishermen were still out in their boats, and the village bell began to ring in alarm.
Someone had to run to the next village for help, but the road was long and the storm was already breaking. 'I will go,' said Ines.
She ran through the rain and the wind, over the hill and across the old bridge, her feet barely touching the ground.
When she reached the next village, she gasped, 'The boats... the storm... help!' The villagers launched their rescue boat at once.
The fishermen were brought safely home, and the whole village cheered for Ines. 'You ran faster than the storm,' they said.
From that day on, Ines was known as the Storm Runner, and whenever the bell rang, everyone knew that help was already on its way.

books.title: The Girl and the Sea Turtle
books.author: Yently Kids
pages: On a quiet beach in summer, a girl called Layla found a sea turtle tangled in an old fishing net.
'Poor turtle,' she said softly. 'Hold still. I will set you free.' Carefully, she cut the net with her pocket scissors.
The turtle looked up at her with wise old eyes, then swam slowly out to sea. Layla watched until it disappeared beneath the waves.
That night, Layla dreamed of the turtle swimming through coral gardens and deep blue caves, free at last.
Every summer after that, Layla returned to the same beach, and every summer she saw a turtle with a small mark on its shell, swimming close to the shore.
'Hello, old friend,' Layla would say, and the turtle would lift its head above the water, as if it remembered her too.
Layla grew up to study the sea, and she spent her life protecting turtles and their beaches, because one small act of kindness had changed everything.

books.title: The Mirror of the Moon
books.author: Yently Kids
pages: Deep in the forest, beside a still lake, there stood a mirror made of silver. It was said that the mirror showed not what you were, but what you could become.
One night, a shy boy named Felix walked to the lake. He was afraid to speak in front of his class, and he wished he could be brave like his older brother.
"Show me who I can be," Felix whispered to the mirror. The surface shimmered, and he saw himself standing on a stage, speaking clearly while a crowd listened and smiled.
Felix returned to the mirror every night. Each time, he saw himself a little braver: asking a question in class, helping a lost child, singing a song for his friends.

One morning, Felix raised his hand in class for the first time. His voice shook, but he spoke, and his classmates listened. He realised the mirror had not changed him — it had only shown him what was already inside.
